about.ai.p: AI assistants (Claude by Anthropic, Codex by OpenAI) were used to write code, run analyses and draft documentation; a local open model (Qwen, via Ollama) translated the interface into the languages other than English and Italian. The harmonisation method and the design choices were selected by the team from the tests; AI was not used to ideate the solution (Space Apps rule).
about.m.1: Harmonised series. "Long": Aqua-equivalent MODIS 1 km detections from 2003-01 (Aqua as observed to 2021-12; VIIRS converted to Aqua units after that and in 2020-08), with 90% intervals. "Detail": VIIRS 375 m detections from 2013-01 at S-NPP level, harmonising S-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21; its band is the spread between satellites, not a confidence interval. The unit is detections, not burned area; FRP is not harmonised.
about.m.2: The harmonised series are monthly: the Day step and single detections are available in the MODIS and VIIRS views only. Values are on 1 degree cells, so a small area counts every cell it overlaps, whole; cell values are noisy, use regional totals for statements.
about.m.4: Sources filter, from the FIRMS type field: 0 vegetation fire, 1 volcano, 2 other static land source, 3 offshore. Single detections follow the filter exactly. The monthly map at global zoom shows vegetation fires only, and so do the harmonised series (static sources are masked with one rule for all sensors).
about.m.5: Harmonisation in short: VIIRS detections of one overpass in a cell of about 1 km are clustered and weighted to mimic what a 1 km MODIS pixel detects; VIIRS is converted to Aqua units with a ratio per 2.5 degree block, calendar month and day/night; calibration uses S-NPP against Aqua in 2013-2020, before the orbit drift of Aqua, and nothing is recalibrated after 2020; the 90% intervals come from out-of-sample residuals, with a drift term after 2020.
about.v.3: Burned area (GFED5) is not used as validation: in 2003-2020 the published long series is almost only Aqua as observed, so a correlation with GFED5 would test Aqua, not the harmonisation.
about.what.p1: Fire Globe was built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, challenge "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots". It turns the MODIS (2000-) and VIIRS (2012-) active-fire records of NASA FIRMS into harmonised series that can be compared across sensors and years, and lets anyone explore them on a 3D globe, for any area, with uncertainty intervals and exports.
badge.harm: MODIS and VIIRS harmonised: one consistent series
basemap.gibs-truecolor: VIIRS NOAA-20 true colour, daily (NASA GIBS)
cal.raw: Raw counts of one sensor. MODIS and VIIRS are not comparable until harmonised.
cal.src.harmDetail: Harmonised detail series, VIIRS 375 m detections at S-NPP level (2013+), 1 degree cells. The band is the spread between satellite pairs, not a confidence interval.
cal.src.harmLong: Harmonised long-term series, Aqua-equivalent detections on 1 degree cells overlapping the area. 2003-2021 measured by Aqua; from 2022 (and Aug 2020) converted from VIIRS, with a 90% interval.
cal.types.harm: Not applicable: the harmonised series are built on vegetation fires only

ctl.sources.harm: Not applicable: the harmonised series are built on vegetation fires only
ex.datasets.cdDetections: Harmonised monthly detections (0 when the region has no row that month)
ex.datasets.docHarmGrid: Harmonised detections on a 1 degree grid, per month. Long-term (Aqua-equivalent) or detail (VIIRS 375 m) series.
ex.datasets.docRegions: Harmonised monthly detections by country or GFED region, with the usual value (median of the same calendar month in the other years), ratio, percentile and signal. Months without a row had 0 detections and are counted as 0.
ex.datasets.errNoRegions: No harmonised regional data in this build.
